abstract: The pursuit of designing high-performance thermoelectric (TE) materials is often hindered by the complex coupling between structural composition and transport properties. In this study, we present TE-Diffusion, an inverse design framework combining a generative diffusion model with a novel three-channel doping representation designed to capture subtle stoichiometric variations intrinsic to complex doping. Comprehensive evaluations demonstrate that TE-Diffusion significantly outperforms traditional generative adversarial networks (GANs).
